subject: Post-demo: reserved pool scope, isolation, fallbacks
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Cheng <alyssa@polarisbio.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: reserved pool scope, isolation, fallbacks

Hi Alyssa —

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap of what I heard and the pieces we should align on before the technical deep-dive: 

- Primary pain: inference cost volatility and noisy-tenancy impacting tail latency for your clinical scoring models.
- Desired outcome: dedicated/reserved GPU pool with strong tenant isolation, predictable p99 latency for 2k token requests, and an ops playbook for burst traffic during nightly re-scoring windows.
- Scale targets: baseline 4x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved (steady), burst to 8 GPUs for 2 hours nightly.
- SLAs: 99.9% uptime target for the pool; p99 latency target ~350ms for standard prompt profile (we'll validate in tech call).
- Security & compliance: must pass basic questionnaire (we captured SOC2 + encryption-at-rest) and data residency requirement in us-west.

Next steps I propose: 
1) I’ll share a draft SOW + resource plan for your internal review (attached).
2) Schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive with your infra & ML infra teams to validate latency profile and deployment topology (suggest July 6–8).
3) Procurement: confirm PO timeline so we can hold the reserved slots (we can provision a canary pool earlier if you need immediate isolation).

Would you and procurement be okay with the PO timing if we target a July 15 start? If that’s tight, we can push a short-term reserved canary for one week while the contract is finalized.

Attachments: [Attachment: SOW-draft.pdf (PDF, 42KB)], [Attachment: resource-plan.xlsx (Excel, 24KB)]

Thanks — I’ll loop Ben and Naomi for ops and pricing details below.

—
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference
From: Alyssa Cheng <alyssa@polarisbio.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@polarisbio.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 18:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: reserved pool scope, isolation, fallbacks

Thanks Rishi — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Confirmed: baseline reserve of 4 GPUs with ability to burst to 8 for the nightly window. We may need a second burst window on weekly retrain nights but that’s later stage.
- SLA: 99.9% uptime is acceptable; for p99 latency we want a guaranteed target for the most common prompt bucket (1k–2k tokens). We’ll send a sample of real prompt distributions ahead of the tech call.
- Security: we’ll send the questionnaire back by EOD Friday; our compliance team will want a brief on data encryption and key management.
- Procurement timeline: we can aim for PO by July 12 if we have the SOW and rate card this week.

Can we confirm the tech deep-dive for July 7 at 11am PT? That works for the infra + ML infra folks.

On the canary pool — yes please. If you can provision a 1–2 GPU isolated canary next week (read-only traffic), we’ll route a small percentage to validate latency and model parity.

Best,
Alyssa
Director of ML Infrastructure
Polaris Bio
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Cheng <alyssa@polarisbio.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 09:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: reserved pool scope, isolation, fallbacks

On Thu, Jul 1, 2027 at 9:05 AM Alyssa Cheng <alyssa@polarisbio.com> wrote:
> Can we confirm the tech deep-dive for July 7 at 11am PT?

Confirmed — booking invite sent for Jul 7 11:00–12:00 PT. Agenda we’ll cover: topology options (single tenant pool vs shared with strict scheduling), KV/prefix caching behavior, quantization tradeoffs (latency vs quality), and ops runbook for burst scaling and failover.

Operational notes: 
- Canary provisioning: we can stand up a 2-GPU canary in us-west by July 5 (READ-ONLY routing, prefix/KV cache warmers).
- Fallbacks: we recommend configuring a cost-tier fallback to a medium-latency model family in another region if capacity constrained; we’ll document exact routing policy for the SOW.

Naomi — can you attach the preliminary rate card and estimated monthly run rate for the baseline + burst scenario?

—
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Cheng <alyssa@polarisbio.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: reserved pool scope, isolation, fallbacks

Adding the rate summary here as promised (attached in the Drive link for full spreadsheet). High level: 

- Baseline (4 GPU reserved, 24/7): estimated $28,500 / month (includes reserved compute + support).
- Burst (additional 4 GPUs for 2 hours nightly): incremental charge ~ $6,200 / month (time-windowed burst pricing).
- One-week canary (2 GPUs): $1,100 flat for the week.

I’ve also included two optional mitigations that reduce run rate by ~20%: 16-bit quantization profile validated for your models, and prefix caching for stable prefixes during scoring. We’ll validate quality impact in the tech call.

Next steps: Rishi will send a short SOW with the routing/fallback policy + timeline. Ben will run the canary provisioning, and Alyssa/procurement will confirm PO timing (target July 12).

Thanks —
Naomi Feldman
Head of Customer Pricing, Redwood Inference
